November 26, 2026 — a note from the sky, and from the data.

Today: the Moon sextile Mars.

Run the exact same rules against a sky shifted by a year or more, a hundred times over. At three years the fake sky scores 53.16% and the real one 53.15% — a gap of −0.01 points (p = 0.981). A counterfeit sky keeps pace with the real one. The apparent edge is seasonality wearing a costume.

That is the point of the whole exercise: to state plainly where classical market astrology does not beat a coin toss. The full study — methods and code — is published in the open.
